title: Unchecked Local Config Override Drift
damaged_code:
```bash
# Manual edits on individual production nodes bypass source control
ssh node_4 "echo 'pool_size: 40' >> /etc/app/config.yaml"
```
pattern: Modifying configuration variables locally on specific live servers or database instances by hand.
why_bad: Results in configuration drift, creating "snowflake" servers. It creates silent operational bugs where node 1 behaves differently than node 4 under the same workload, causing diagnostic nightmares.
detection: A horizontally scaled cluster where local configuration properties files contain mismatching checksums across nodes.
counterexample: Deploying configurations strictly via central automation (like Ansible or Terraform) verified by source control commit histories.
fix: Treat configuration files as read-only; enforce all changes through centralized orchestration tools, auditing checksums continuously to block manual drift.
source: [Pragmatic Programmers] Michael T. Nygard - *Release It!_ Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software* (2007, Pragmatic Bookshelf).pdf, Section 14.2.
